account: Something unusual is being arranged at the town hall, apparently a feast or community celebration. I saw the builder and innkeeper put bread in a hall table chest yesterday, and lanterns were already placed. Today the baker told me the innkeeper had verified delivery of two hundred feast loaves. The builder has now invited me to the hall at eighteen, with the innkeeper escorting me, but explicitly asked to keep the occasion's details secret until then. The secretary says the innkeeper described it as community hospitality, with the programme announced at eighteen and no prepared remarks needed. I suspect a friendly surprise celebration, possibly for me, though I have no confirmation of its purpose. The builder, innkeeper and baker are involved in the arrangements; the secretary has been checking on them without learning the occasion. There are also repeated rumours about a bridge or port change at the bakery, but the baker has verified no bridge or ferry change, so I should not treat those repetitions as evidence. My scheduled office business has been unusually thin: no council letters arrived today, and yesterday no accounts were available. I cannot establish that this is connected to the gathering. I kept my morning office and mill appointments, although I still lack a proper grain-stock report. I have now reached the neighbour's east-bank cottage early for our fifteen o'clock tea. Afterwards I have the sixteen-thirty office appointment and the newly confirmed eighteen o'clock hall invitation.
